a_problem: AI agents built most of your product. It seems to work. For now.
a_want: You want to feel confident your foundations will hold as you grow.
b_problem: Agents connect your CRM, ERP and reports, and the AI bill grows every month.
b_want: You want lower AI costs without having to learn yet another system.
a_get_title: You keep shipping. I make sure it holds.
a_get_body: I build a picture of how your product is actually put together: architecture, dependencies, operations and where it's fragile. I ask the questions you didn't know you needed to ask. Then we fix what won't hold and set up guardrails so your agents stop repeating the same mistakes. You keep the speed and can scale with confidence.
a_get_aside: AI agents are crazy fast and build exactly what you ask for. I know what the code needs to look like for it to stay that fast a year from now.
a_get_step: The first step is a review at a fixed price. You get a written report that's yours, whatever you decide next.
b_get_title: Same workflows. A fraction of the AI bill.
b_get_body: Your agents are reading the same invoice for the hundredth time, and you pay for every read. I find what they do over and over again and streamline the flow. AI is used only where real judgement is needed. Same job as today, only cheaper and faster. And nothing new for you to learn.
b_get_aside: How much you can save depends entirely on how your workflows look. That's why we start with a review: you get it in black and white what costs what and what can be slimmed down, before you decide anything.
